{"id": "fc307ec6-be4e-4a52-ada4-349c8112f650", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "thinking", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "I'm calculating monthly costs from the fixture data: EC2 m6g.large at $65.70/month, EBS gp3 30GB at $2.70/month, and now working through DynamoDB provisioned capacity costs with 20 RCU and 20 WCU.

I need to account for the free tier, which covers 25 units of capacity translating to 18600 unit-hours/month based on 744 hours (31-day month). This raises the question of whether to use 730 or 744 hours per month for consistency with the free tier calculation, so I'm working out both approaches.

With provisioned capacity at 20 RCU and 20 WCU, under either 744 or 730 hours/month, the total usage stays below the 18600 unit-hour free tier threshold since 20 is less than the 25-unit free allowance. So the entire DynamoDB usage falls within the free tier, meaning the table cost comes out to $0/month for this table, based on the given pricing fixture.

Totaling it up: EC2 at $65.70, EBS gp3 at $2.70, and DynamoDB at $0, giving roughly $68.40/month overall. I want to flag assumptions clearly — 730 hrs/month, on-demand pricing since no commitment info was given, and that real AWS pricing lookups weren't available so this relies on the fixture price data provided.

DynamoDB stays free-tier so no added cost there, and since the pricing API is unavailable as expected, I'll rely on the fixture data provided and answer directly without needing any tool calls.

"}]}
